lines.trans: My mother's intuition keeps tingling—I swear that front-building senior has fallen head over heels for our Seung-chan!
Blame me—I had no business giving birth to such a dazzling son! One glance and he drips with aristocratic elegance!
Senior, the cleaners said the outdoor AC unit was excluded, so I scrubbed the whole thing myself!
And talk about brains—the boy is so smart and scholarly!
You must memorize these carefully and never mix them up! The yellow cloth is for the bathroom, and the blue one is for the wood floor.
And this one is for furniture, the kitchen sink cloth, balcony glass, and this one is for wiping the sofa!
How on earth did you memorize all six of those?! Hey, you can stop waxing the floor now!
Not at all—I can keep polishing plenty more!
Heavy labor like moving furniture is for your father—what would our delicate Seung-chan know about chores like that?

meanings.note: Used in -(으)ㄴ/는 것 같다 to express 'it seems that...' or 'I think...'.

meanings.note: Honorific equivalent of 있다; used in 안녕히 계세요 ('goodbye' to someone staying).

그러다.gloss: to say so; to do so

meanings.en: to say so; to speak like that

meanings.en: to do so; to act like that

examples.trans: Who said that?

그렇다.gloss: to be so, to do so

examples.trans: Is that really so?
Don't keep acting like that.
I bought bread. And I bought milk too.
Let's eat and then depart.

meanings.note: When used with 알다/모르다, it means knowing or not knowing a fact or how to do something.

examples.trans: I knew it would rain.

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?

examples.text: 머리는 또 좀 좋으냐고, 애가 아주 스마트하고 학구적이어서!
